## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D pixelated side-view battle royale simulation where 20 independently-thinking survivors gather supplies, craft, build, and fight while the player observes.

## Requirements
- Phone/tablet-friendly 2D game with smooth animations; the player simply watches.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks (viewport no wider than 1280px); inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Built a self-contained canvas game with a responsive observer dashboard, rather than introducing a framework or dependencies.
- Survivors autonomously scavenge, eat, craft weapons/armor, build, fight, and can be followed by tapping/clicking them.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game UI, responsive styling, canvas wilderness art, 20 autonomous survivors, supplies, combat, crafting/building, event feed, follow mode, pause/speed controls, sorting, and restart.
- `node --check game.js` passed; local server returned HTTP 200.
- Browser check confirmed 20 roster entries and simulation running; inspected desktop and mobile screenshots at `screenshots/latest.jpg`.
- Added a data-URI favicon after browser reported a missing `/favicon.ico`.

### Active
- Review/fix any remaining gameplay or presentation issues, then summarize assumptions and completion for the user.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect latest changes and verify `node --check game.js`.
2. Optionally rerun browser smoke check and save/inspect `screenshots/latest.jpg`.
3. Give the user a concise completion note with assumptions and how to play.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game page structure and dashboard.
- `style.css`: Desktop/mobile styling and touch-friendly layout.
- `game.js`: Simulation, rendering, controls, and survivor AI.
- `screenshots/latest.jpg`: Most recent mobile screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; repository also had unrelated untracked files before this work.
- A Python server was launched with `python3 -m http.server 3000 --bind 0.0.0.0`.
- Browser screenshot at 1280×900 showed the game; mobile check used 390×844.
- Last edits added arrow ownership and hid the season tag on small screens; a subsequent identical edit attempt to `game.js` failed with “No changes to apply,” so no change resulted from that attempt.
